description: Change a workflow you own (or your team owns): title, description, tags and/or its whole step graph. Read it with get_workflow first and send the full edited `contents`, plus that call's `updatetime` as `loaded_updatetime` so a newer save by someone else is not overwritten. Leave metadata.input.values out to keep the saved input values; a value shown as [hidden] is restored from the saved workflow. Everyone who can open the workflow can read its saved values, so never save a key or password in one. Wiro checks and prepares the new graph like create_workflow, with the same 40 KB limit on the new graph, also when the saved workflow is larger (removing steps can bring it under). Replacing the steps cannot be undone: without `confirm: true` the call checks the new graph, reports any problems and the defaults it filled, and returns what would change, saving nothing; show it to the user and repeat the call with `confirm: true` after they agree. Editing a published workflow takes it out of the public gallery until Wiro reviews it again, so that also needs `acknowledge_review_reset: true`.

acknowledge_review_reset.description: Required to edit a published workflow, after the user agreed it leaves the gallery until reviewed.

confirm.description: Required to save new `contents`, after the user approved the change summary.

contents.description: The workflow graph (version "1"): {version, nodes, output, schema, metadata}. Read get_playbook topic "workflow-graph" for the format and an example.

force.description: Overwrite a newer version. Only when the user explicitly wants that.

loaded_updatetime.description: The `updatetime` from get_workflow (or the last update). Protects against overwriting newer changes.

slug.description: The full workflow slug or the workflow page URL.

name: update_workflow

stepChanges.description: What changed inside each step of stepsChanged. Input values are JSON text with object keys sorted and secrets hidden; null means not set. A long value is cut around the first place where the old and new value differ, with ... where text is left out.

discarded.description: With unchanged: Start field changes Wiro does not keep, because it saves Start fields the way the wiro.ai editor writes them.

required.description: Whether a run must be given this input, as far as Wiro says. Left out when that is not known.

title: Update a Wiro workflow
